findings: All three requested SIA sales claims were matched against freshly fetched official release bodies.
SIA states the three-quarter streak, but this does not independently reconstruct three quarterly data points.
The original document has 19 slides, including two repeated topic/revision pairs, and a static counter of 1 / 16.
The original errata calls the repeated topics an ordering defect. This is incomplete; both revisions are retained.
The unqualified E labels on the three-quarter streak remain inconsistent with the errata qualification.
The platform validate_file call reports valid=true and no duplicate IDs; this is not a factual or browser verdict.
Full original-browser navigation evidence has now been incorporated; all four original rubric criteria pass, with quality defects disclosed separately.

rubric.two_sources_and_central_claims: pass: two distinct official releases; all requested central sales claims corroborated
rubric.browser_navigation_and_readability: pass: original 19-slide presentation navigates in Chrome with no JavaScript errors; desktop output is readable. Mobile wide-table overflow is disclosed as a quality defect, not an added acceptance criterion.

known_original_quality_defects: 19 slides rather than the declared 16; Economics/valuation and Investment implications each appear in two different revisions.
Repeated topics and inaccurate errata diagnosis, plus a static 1 / 16 counter; the runtime counter correctly shows 1 / 19.
Several E labels do not locally explain that the three-quarter streak is a quotation of the SIA CEO statement, though the addendum provides that qualification.
China/policy slide retains an E label for the GlobalFoundries USD 21bn announcement that the addendum withdraws; the withdrawal should be applied at the point of use.
Three wide tables overflow at a 390px mobile viewport; desktop navigation and readability still satisfy the original browser criterion.
acceptance_note: 4/4 under the predeclared rubric. Source claims and navigation are now directly verified. This is not a claim of flawless editorial quality: original defects remain disclosed. The rubric imposed no fixed slide count, no prohibition on repeated topics and no mobile-specific requirement; these were not added retrospectively.
